content:
anya: quick question — in staging proxy logs are we still truncating Authorization headers, or do we need to switch to a non-reversible hash? trying to figure out what SRE needs for debug access.

sam: short answer: switch to HMAC(SHA256) with a per-deployment salt stored in KMS. truncation leaks enough to be risky.

kevin: +1. hashing lets us correlate requests without exposing token material. salt kept in KMS and rotated. SRE should get a read-only ability to compute/compare hashes, not the raw salt.

security-bot: POLICY: Authorization headers must be redacted or pseudonymized in logs. Reversible storage of tokens is prohibited. Exceptions require an approved security exception ticket.

leo: @kevin the HMAC approach is fine but flagging perf — dedicated proxy handles ~10k rps on some routes. we should avoid sync HMAC in the hot path if possible.

sam: perf idea: compute quick prefix-hash (first 8 bytes -> hex) inline for routing/quick correlation, then enqueue full HMAC async to the log writer. or sample full HMAC for high-qps routes. example: `hmac_sha256(salt, token) -> hex` and we write that to logs instead of token.

anya: proposed plan: 1) replace truncation with HMAC-SHA256(salt, token) in staging behind a feature-flag; 2) async HMAC writer + 1% sampling for extremely high-qps routes in prod/dedicated; 3) document exception flow and who can access hash-compare keys. @kevin @leo lmk if that covers concerns.

kevin: sgtm. add KMS rotation schedule and a short note on who can request access (sec-ops + one oncall).

leo: sgtm :thumbsup: also add a metric for HMAC write latency and a flag to disable HMAC sampling if latency spike detected.

security-bot: REQ: create a short PRD + security review ticket referencing policy id SEC-LOG-05 and include sampling rationale.

anya: will write the PRD and open the ticket today, will ping @sec-ops once filed. thanks everyone!
